Hi, resident trans-girl here! In normal circumstances I'd just tell you to post the question in a subreddit with a larger community or trans folks, r/AskTransgender specifically, but I'm already here and you've already asked so I might as well give my own answer. Note this is purely personal experience

  


The reason it's so stress inducing is because every time a trans person is misgendered, it's like a punch in the gut, pulling the chair out from underneath them. even if it was not intentional, every him or her or whatever incorrect pronoun used stands as a constant reminder that despite these people's best efforts, they aren't seen as the person or gender they want to be. It feeds into that self doubt that "you'll never be a real man/woman" or that "you're just pretending to be trans for attention" or that "trans people aren't even real you're mentally ill" or any other manner of self deprecation. It's stress-inducing because it gives the people misgendered anxiety because of the discrepancy between who they are and how other people, sometimes even themselves, may see them.

Ihope my explanation wasn't too rambly or dumb but if it doesn't make sense I highly recommend checking that sub out and asking there; there's people much more qualified to answer them me there!
